title: Malagasy Cinema: The 1970s–1980s
description: The decade and a half following Madagascar's popular revolution of 1972 produced some of the country's most enduring films. A generation of filmmakers who had trained abroad returned with both skills and urgency, working with limited means to bring Malagasy stories to national and international screens. Benoît Ramampy's L'Accident (1972) was the first Malagasy film to appear at FESPACO; Raymond Rajaonarivelo's Tabataba (1988) became the first selected for Cannes. This era established the foundations on which subsequent Malagasy filmmaking rests.
